doorFamilies:
Block names follow '<Revit family> - <type>-<element id or V#>-LEVEL n GENERAL ARRANGEMENT'. The id is the first instance and is reused by identical instances: for example 2330559 serves 4 doors across the two levels. V# marks a geometry variant (flipped hand). There are 40 door inserts, 16 on L1 and 24 on L2, and none is mirrored. Apart from the two pivot panels, every block is inserted at the centre of its wall gap on the wall centre line: all 38 sit within 1 mm of the key centre, along the wall and across it. The block x axis runs along the wall, and the rotation is the wall direction, plus or minus 180 degrees for the swing side.

(1) DOOR_GEN_SWING_1 PANEL_FLUSH - <W>x2400 _black_ (base-building link): L1 3 (1200 B1-15, 900 B1-16, 700 B1-01), L2 1 (700 B2-23). W is the leaf width. The frames are 50 mm, so gap = W + 0.100 (1.300 / 1.000 / 0.800).
(2) _GEN_LIFT_DOOR - DOOR1100x2400 (link): L1 1, L2 1 (B1-05, B2-22). W is the structural opening, 1.100. It slides (no arc), the frame pieces sit inside the opening, and the insert is at the centre of the 150 mm shaft wall.
(3) DOOR-CW_PIVOT_1 PANEL_FLUSH4 - D3 - PL03 (link, curtain-wall door panels): L1 has 2 blocks that make one double opening, B1-08. The name carries no size or height. Each block is one pivot leaf (0.725 / 0.678 swing) inserted at its own panel centre, 0.36 / 0.39 m either side of the slot centre. The slot is 1.503 between the curtain-wall mullions, 1.603 with them.
(4) SINGLE SWING DOOR-GENERIC - <W>X2400 (interior host model): 1000X2400 on L1 x3 (B1-02, B1-04, B1-13) and L2 x3 (B2-07, B2-09, B2-24); 700X2400 on L1 x1 (B1-14). Here W is the wall gap itself: the frame spans +-W/2 with 50 mm frames inside, and the leaf is W - 0.100.
(5) SINGLE GLASS SWING DOOR-GENERIC - TYPE 1 (host): L1 4 (B1-09 to B1-12), L2 1 (B2-25). No size or height, and the block is a leaf only, with no frame. In the facade curtain wall (B1-09) the leaf is 0.875, the slot 0.925 between 50 mm mullions and 1.025 with them. In the glass partitions the leaf is 0.825, 0.875 between the 25 mm jamb mullions and 0.925 between the glass-wall ends. On L2 the leaf is 0.850 and the gap 0.900.
(6) DOUBLE GLASS SWING DOOR-GENERIC - TYPE 1 (host): L1 2. B1-06 has 2 x 0.800 leaves, a 1.600 gap in a frameless 10 mm screen. B1-07 has 2 x 0.787 leaves: 1.575 between the jamb mullions, 1.625 between the glass walls.
(7) DOOR_SWING_1_SOLID - D00-<W>X2400_SW_HD-F_HM-1 (link): L2 6. The 720 type x5 (B2-01, 02, 03, 05, 06) has its leaf drawn at 0.700 and a 0.780 gap; the 900 type x1 (B2-10) has a 0.900 leaf and a 0.980 gap. Gap = leaf + 0.080 (40 mm frames), so the name width is the leaf except for the 720 type.
(8) DOOR_SWING_1_louver - D00-600X2400_SW_HD-F_HM-1 (link): L2 2 (B2-16, B2-18). Leaf 0.600, gap 0.680.
(9) DOOR_SWING_2_SOLID - 800x2000_INT (link): L2 2 (B2-08, B2-21). W is each of the two leaves, so gap = 2W + 0.080 = 1.680.
(10) DOOR_SWING_louver - <W>x2000_INT (link): L2 8. The 650 type x6 (B2-12 to 15, B2-17, B2-20) gives 1.380, the 800 type x1 (B2-11) gives 1.680 and the 900 type x1 (B2-19) gives 1.880. W is each leaf, so gap = 2W + 0.080.

Rule for a detector: the name width equals the wall gap only for the host generic family (4) and the lift door (2). For the base-building families it is the leaf: single doors are leaf + 0.06 to 0.10, double doors are 2 x leaf + 0.08. Glass and pivot doors carry no size, so take the gap from the block geometry; their insert is still the gap centre. Heights come from the name: 2400 for single doors, 2000 for the doubles and louvred doors, none for glass and pivot doors. Not doors: the Q-CASE 'PANEL_ADJ_GEN - ADJUSTABLE CUPBOARD DOOR' blocks (20 on L1, 8 on L2) and the A-DOOR lines inside IA_J12_CABINET.
stairsAndFloorHeight:
The east stair hall (x 1.37-4.55, y 7.0-10.0) holds the only stair inside the bank that links L1 and L2. Every going is 0.25 m.

L1 (solid lines on S-STRS are below the cut, dashed lines on S-STRS-MBND are above it):
- Flight 1 runs north at x 3.27-4.21. Its risers are at y 7.88 / 8.13 / 8.38 / 8.63, so 4 risers, ending at a 0.94 m square landing.
- Flight 2 runs west on y 8.62-9.62. Its risers are at x 3.27 / 3.02 / 2.77 / 2.52 / 2.27, so 5 risers. The cut zigzag sits on the 6th riser from the floor. It ends at the NW landing.
- Flight 3 runs south, with risers at y 8.62 / 8.37 / 8.12, so 3 risers, ending at the SW landing (x 1.39-2.53, y 7.03-8.12).
- Flight 3 and both landings pass over the L1 toilet, which is why they are dashed. L1 has no UP or DOWN text.

L2: the flight that leaves that landing is drawn solid with the DOWN arrow. It runs from x 2.53 to 4.53 on y 7.01-8.16, with risers at x 2.53, 2.78, ... 4.53, so 9 risers (8 goings), and lands on L2 at x 4.53. Its first riser is exactly L1's landing edge at x 2.529.

L1 to L2 is therefore 4 + 5 + 3 + 9 = 21 risers (17 goings and 3 landings). The UP arrow on L2 starts the next stair: a north flight of 9 risers, a west landing, then 9 risers back east above flight 4, 18 risers in all to the floor above.

The straight stair drawn outside the north wall (18 risers on 0.20 m goings, cut on L1, all below the cut on L2) has no door into the bank on either floor. I used it only as a cross-check: at the same height its risers would be about 0.20 m, which is normal for an old shophouse stair.

Riser used: 0.175 m, the top of the normal commercial range.
- The drawn going is 0.25 m, so 2R + G = 0.60 m, the comfortable minimum. With 0.17 it would be 0.59.
- Revit takes the fewest risers that keep each riser under the stair type's maximum. Under the usual 0.18 m maximum for non-residential stairs (with a going of at least 0.25 m, the Thai rule as I recall it), 21 risers means 3.60 < floor-to-floor <= 3.78 m. 0.175 fits that; 0.17 would give 3.57 m, where 20 risers would have been enough.

Floor-to-floor = 21 x 0.175 = 3.675, rounded to 3.70 m. Caveat: if the architect kept Revit's default metric stair type (190 mm maximum riser, 250 mm going, and the going does match), the real height could be 3.80-3.99 m. Expose 3.70 m as an editable default.
alignment:
Yes. Both levels share one origin, and the offset is (0, 0).
- Grid: the 30 S-GRID lines are identical on both levels to 0.1 mm. The bubbles sit at exactly the same points (dx = dy = 0.0000): A / B / C at x -5.0804 / 0.8546 / 6.7346, and 1 to 7 at y -9.030 / -6.520 / -3.410 / 0.000 / 3.300 / 6.865 / 11.605. The dimension strings match.
- Lift: door block 2145865 is at (-1.5554, -7.6300) on both levels, and the shaft walls sit on the same x faces (-3.58, -3.48, -3.43, -1.63, -1.48). Only the shaft's north wall differs, by 23 mm, because it was modelled per level.
- Columns: the five columns on grid A match to 0.000 (one is off by 6 mm). The grid-B columns differ by 10-34 mm, being separate instances per level. The east columns differ because each level uses a different column size behind a different facade.
- Stairs: the outside north stair's 18 riser lines are at the same x on both levels. The east stair's dashed L1 landing edge (x 2.529) is exactly the first riser of the flight drawn on L2, and the west landing is at x 1.373 on L1 and 1.375 on L2.
- Shared door: the base-building door block 2146164 is at (-3.9804, -6.730) on L1 and (-3.9804, -6.7395) on L2, because its wall is 9.5 mm apart between the levels.
Both files are views of one Revit model in shared coordinates, with the origin on grid line 4 (y = 0). No shift or rotation is needed.
conversionCheck:
The project DWGs are byte-identical (sha256) to the copies that were converted. I dumped both DWGs afresh with dwgread -O JSON into my folder and compared them with the DXFs, read by ezdxf (ezdxf audit errors: 0).

Counts:
- Entities: L1 4473 / 4473, L2 21581 / 21581. Every type is equal: LINE, ARC, SPLINE, INSERT, LWPOLYLINE, HATCH, MTEXT, ELLIPSE, CIRCLE, DIMENSION, IMAGE, VIEWPORT.
- Layers: all 35 / 33 layers are equal.
- Model space flattened the way the tool reads it (blocks unpacked): L1 6120 / 6120, L2 23507 / 23507, with 0 differing (layer, type) cells.
- L1: A-WALL 343 (LINE 296, HATCH 36, INSERT 11), A-WALL-PATT 35, A-DOOR 123 (16 INSERT, 90 LINE, 17 ARC), A-DOOR-FRAM 54, A-DOOR-GLAZ 24, A-DOOR-HDLN 6, A-GLAZ-CURT 48, A-GLAZ-CWMG 199.
- L2: A-WALL 355 (LINE 309, HATCH 26, ARC 12, INSERT 6, SPLINE 2), A-WALL-PATT 42, A-DOOR 216 (24 INSERT), A-DOOR-FRAM 235, A-DOOR-GLAZ 4, A-DOOR-HDLN 1. L2 has no A-GLAZ layers in the DWG either.
- No UNKNOWN objects. All 5244 / 22461 object-map handles were decoded.

Level 2's 8 errors are 4 + 4 inside two MTEXT on G-ANNO-TEXT, 'UP' (handle 67A3) and 'DOWN' (67A4). They come from the background-mask fields (bg_fill_flag 3: 'bit_read_BL code 11', 'invalid CMC flag 0x43 / method 0'). The text, insertion point, layer and style were read before the error, the CRC checks pass, and both labels are in the DXF at (4.679, 9.521) and (4.679, 7.651). Only the mask colour of two labels is lost. Nothing that matters is lost.

The warnings are harmless on both levels:
- 'Object handle not found' (L1 28, L2 20): back-references from the '_Oblique' arrowhead block to dimension-tick inserts that Revit never wrote. That is 2 per dimension; the DIMBLOCKs hold their ticks as lines.
- 'Skip HATCH common handles' (L1 148, L2 143): one per hatch. Boundaries, fills and layers are all read.
- MATERIAL / TABLESTYLE / MLEADERSTYLE class warnings: not geometry.

Decision F's count check passes for both files, and the LibreDWG DXFs are safe to use.
